reasons.A: Short, punchy declaratives and a plain, assertive stance ('That is all it can be', 'almost any method will do') are far from the passage's long, qualified, periodic sentences.
reasons.B: Long, balanced sentences with measured hedging ('It would seem to follow', 'rather little', 'It may help') and a composed, reflective stance match the passage's movement and tone most closely without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Right register and long clauses, but it stacks the author's hedges and devices ('It seems to me', 'arguably', 'in some sense', a triple-semicolon series, question opener) more thickly than the passage does, so it reads as imitation.
